Remote monitoring:an evaluation of implantable devices for management of heart failure patients REM-HF

The aim of the study is to determine the clinical and cost-effectiveness of these remote disease management devices, using specialist nurses to monitor and initiate delivery of interventions compared to usual care in patients with severe chronic heart failure. 

The second aim of the study is to evaluate patient and carer satisfaction of implanted monitoring devices for heart failure management

texts.c22cbdcd3e72: There is today a pressing need to develop new ways of managing the rapidly increasing number of people living with heart failure in the UK. For patients who already have implantable devices, remote monitoring of heart failure using automated implanted devices and bespoke care pathways/protocols to give early warning of deterioration and facilitate pre-emptive action may be an important solution to the dual problem of increasing healthcare need but with static (or reducing) healthcare resource. The REM-HF study randomises a typical population of patients with heart failure who have implanted devices capable of being monitored remotely to either protocol-driven care informed by weekly remote monitoring, or to "usual" care. The aim of the study is to determine the clinical and cost-effectiveness of these remote disease management devices, using specialist nurses to monitor and initiate delivery of interventions compared to usual care in patients with severe chronic heart failure. The second aim of the study is to evaluate patient and carer satisfaction of implanted monitoring devices for heart failure management
